title: Cambridge T-S K5.7 — Hebrew cipher border and unresolved interior

documents.shelfmark: Cambridge University Library, Taylor-Schechter Collection, T-S K5.7, recto (PGP 42030)

plaintext.source: Bohak (2010), pp. 13–15, reads the Hebrew border.

transcription.source: Bohak's upper-letter transcription and a masked classification of lower marks from Cambridge's recto photograph.
transcription.notes: The register distinguishes 98 extant positions and seven losses. The tokenization of the lower signs remains open.

system.summary: Published Hebrew substitution values recover the vertical border. The interior rule is unknown.

diacritics.note: Small marks beneath the upper signs include dots, strokes and rings. Their function is uncertain.

system.sibling_key: Bohak's sign table for T-S K24.19, figure 3.

prior_solution.where: Gideon Bohak, Cracking the Code and Finding the Gold (2010), pp. 13–15.

conditions.human_role: Identified the target and supplied the photograph and published study.

solution.what: Registered published upper readings and classified lower-mark crops with positions masked.
Measured the minimum cell changes required for one alphabet per row, allowing every interior omission in row 2.
Tested the T-S Misc.22.218 sequence on grid routes and under secondary substitutions.

outcome.notes: The published border reading is prior work. No interior plaintext has been recovered.
